# BALANITIS AND BALANOPOSTHITIS

Balanitis is inflammation of the glans penis and is often associated with erythema and pruritis. When the foreskin is also involved, the condition is known as balanoposthitis (also referred to as balanitis in this discussion).

There are a variety of causes of balanitis, but most are due to poor hygiene of the foreskin in uncircumcised men resulting in candida infection. Other, less common causes, include bacterial infection (typically sexually transmitted or anaerobic bacteria), dermatologic conditions, malignancy as well as others. Men with Candidal balanitis often have a white curd-like exudate compared to a thick foul-smelling purulent exudate in menu with anaerobic bacterial balanitis.

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for treatment:
[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](sexually-transmitted-infection)

Therapy:
## Candidal balanitis empirical treatment

## Inpatient

### Mild to moderate cases

Preferred:
Clotrimazole 1% cream topically q12h ($) [M] for 7 days

Alternative:
Nystatin cream 100,000 units/g cream topically q12h ($) [M] for 7 days

### Severe cases

Fluconazole 150 mg PO once ($) [R,DI]

### Bacterial balanitis empirical treatment

### Mild cases

Metronidazole 0.75% cream topically q12h ($)[DI] for 7 days

### Moderate to severe cases

Metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 7 days
